NATIVE-001.summary: Lifecycle commands use the published rer package.
NATIVE-001.was: Commands ran through the bundled node scripts/rer.mjs entry point.
NATIVE-001.now: Commands run through rer; local setup still stops its runtime, dev opens the local owner automatically, and deployment dry-run makes no provider requests.

FIRST-RUN-001.summary: New workspaces are provisioned with a starter assistant and installation mail settings, with a smaller first-run form.
FIRST-RUN-001.was: First-run led to a setup checklist and ordinary workspace creation led with the widget snippet.
FIRST-RUN-001.now: One-screen setup derives optional names and colours. Non-demo workspaces gain a default starter assistant, a mailbox when INBOUND_EMAIL_TOKEN exists and the installation sender until their domain is verified. Explicit creation may send one welcome email; uncertain mail is never replayed. Setup separates owner-only tasks from provisioned settings.

ACTIVATION-001.summary: Setup observes applicable steps automatically and supports durable owner/admin skips.
ACTIVATION-001.was: The empty inbox and Setup showed the same eight-step checklist; validation was explicit and publication counted as a step.
ACTIVATION-001.now: Only Setup loads the observations. Signed-in checks perform bounded non-generative reads, never send mail; GET writes nothing. Published articles do not count. Owner-only steps can be skipped without provider work, remain unconfirmed and leave the denominator; an observation wins and rejected keys remain Needs you. Observation details can be stored without backfilling old receipts.

AI-001.summary: A starter assistant without its provider key leaves new conversations with the team.
AI-001.was: Missing providers failed explicitly when model execution was requested.
AI-001.now: Requested model execution still fails explicitly without a provider; new conversations do not assign a default assistant whose provider has no key. Uncertain attempts remain uncertain and daily ceilings still apply.

IDENTITY-003.summary: Mailbox confirmation covers new and existing accounts with unknown passwords.
IDENTITY-003.was: Moved-in teammates and email-claimed owners encountered a password-only step-up.
IDENTITY-003.now: Accounts without a second factor can confirm beside their password by a single-use, 15-minute account-bound email sign-in link. Requests claim shared account/IP rate limits atomically and are audited. Only the fresh mailbox sign-in session gains proof. Recent mailbox proof authorizes replacing an unknown existing password without its old value; a held session cannot. Existing deliberately chosen passwords remain valid. New email claims create no unknown password or recent proof. Every enrolled second-factor gate and recovery rule remains unchanged. Migration 190 admits the distinct email_link proof method while retaining existing session proofs and timestamps.

REPORTS-001.summary: Reports exclude empty drafts and export complete workspace history.
REPORTS-001.was: Analytics counted empty widget conversations and exported no message text.
REPORTS-001.now: Reports and analytical CSVs require a persisted message; the widget session contract is retained. A separate guarded streaming JSON export includes all workspace conversations, messages, private notes and attachment metadata across dates and imports, excluding attachment bytes.

INTEGRATION-001.was: A visitor matching the reply sender was shown no attempt recorded.
INTEGRATION-001.now: Message status explains when the visitor address matches the reply sender; shared recipient selection preserves preferred addresses, participants and recorded delivery outcomes.

agentUpdateInstructions: Update from v0.4.1 to v0.4.2 while preserving owner customizations, native credentials, tenant authority, private settings and human Send. Stop the runtime and back up D1, R2 and Durable Object business state. Install frozen dependencies with @runeditrun/rer 0.2.42. Apply every listed migration in filename order before the updated Worker serves traffic. Never reset to upgrade. Rer deploy claims the configured OWNER_EMAIL for a new installation without choosing a password; the owner signs in by email, and existing owners are preserved. Mailbox links do not bypass any enrolled second factor. First-password installation and sensitive actions require recent proof. Retain uncertain outcomes without replay, reviewed imports and erasure fences. Reports offers full conversation JSON with messages/private notes and attachment names; bytes remain in the portable archive. Preserve all existing qualification limits and the accessibility owner HOLD. An older 0.3 installation follows OPERATIONS.md first.
publicReleaseNotes: HappyToHelp v0.4.2 is the current deployable release. It includes mailbox step-up and first-password setup including existing accounts whose passwords were never known, complete conversation JSON export, honest same-address mail status and Reports that exclude empty widget drafts. It also carries the native two-factor, roles, audit, portable Durable Object, knowledge/feedback and import improvements since v0.4.1. Commands pin @runeditrun/rer 0.2.42; hosted deployment claims the configured owner, who signs in by email. Existing owners and passwords remain. Apply the listed migrations before serving traffic. Provider fixtures establish local protocol behavior only; paid-provider quality, real-vendor compatibility and hosted operating costs remain separately qualified. Accessibility remains on owner HOLD. app.happytohelp.com is separate legacy production.
